name: AB-string
description: The string $$$t_1t_2 \dots t_k$$$ is good if each letter of this string belongs to at least one palindrome of length greater than 1 . A palindrome is a string that reads the same backward as forward. For example, the strings A , BAB , ABBA , BAABBBAAB are palindromes, but the strings AB , ABBBAA , BBBA are not. Here are some examples of good strings: $$$t$$$ = AABBB (letters $$$t_1$$$, $$$t_2$$$ belong to palindrome $$$t_1 \dots t_2$$$ and letters $$$t_3$$$, $$$t_4$$$, $$$t_5$$$ belong to palindrome $$$t_3 \dots t_5$$$); $$$t$$$ = ABAA (letters $$$t_1$$$, $$$t_2$$$, $$$t_3$$$ belong to palindrome $$$t_1 \dots t_3$$$ and letter $$$t_4$$$ belongs to palindrome $$$t_3 \dots t_4$$$); $$$t$$$ = AAAAA (all letters belong to palindrome $$$t_1 \dots t_5$$$); You are given a string $$$s$$$ of length $$$n$$$, consisting of only letters A and B . You have to calculate the number of good substrings of string $$$s$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 3 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the length of the string $$$s$$$. The second line contains the string $$$s$$$, consisting of letters A and B .
output_specification: Print one integer — the number of good substrings of string $$$s$$$.
approach_summary: Apply Knapsack and Basic Dynamic Programming paradigm under the Dynamic Programming (DP) framework. Exploit problem invariants to reduce state space and achieve optimal complexity.
